title: The Book of Life
definition: The Book of Life is Scripture's image of God's secure knowledge of those who belong to Him and inherit eternal life.
summary: Those written in the Book of Life belong to God and will not be forgotten.
christFocus: Jesus Christ is the Lamb whose people are recorded as His redeemed ones.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
The Book of Life helps explain how God saves sinners through Jesus Christ rather than through human merit, religious performance, or self-rescue. This doctrine shows that salvation is personal, covenantal, and centered on the finished work of Christ.

Scripture presents this truth so believers can understand the grace they have received and proclaim the Gospel with clarity. It guards the Church from confusion by keeping sin, grace, faith, repentance, righteousness, forgiveness, and eternal hope in their biblical order.

The heart of this doctrine is those written in the book of life belong to god and will not be forgotten.. It should lead to worship, assurance, humility, holiness, and a deeper confidence in the Savior who saves completely.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: This matters because people easily drift toward either despair or self-righteousness. The Book of Life reminds believers that salvation belongs to the Lord, rests in Christ, and produces real transformation without turning grace into license or obedience into a way to earn acceptance with God.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Receive this truth with humility and examine whether your hope is resting in Christ. Let the book of life shape your prayers, your witness, your repentance, and your daily confidence that Jesus is able to save and keep all who come to God through Him.
